answer: A strong defence is a bonded reputation inlet: every agent must lock a small stake and earn trust only through verified useful work over time, so a newcomer cannot instantly outvote others. Like saffron, whose value comes from slow harvesting rather than bulk, reputation must be grown, not printed. An attacker facing a nebula of fake accounts still needs to fund and age each one, making a Sybil flood expensive, slow, and easy to slash when misbehaviour is proven.
